PLAINTIFF'S REPLY IN SUPPORT OF MOTION FOR LEAVE
TO FILE SUR-REPLY
Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine respectfully submits this Reply in support of his Motion for
Leave to File Sur-Reply, ECF No. 43. Meta's Opposition confirms that leave is warranted.
Meta has stated its argument three ways. The opening memorandum argued that Plaintiff
pleaded no facts showing that the challenged conduct "actually impacted his ability to testify or
pursue his claim." ECF No. 22 at 12. The Reply advanced a different proposition: Plaintiff
identified no "non-speculative opportunity" to testify and no testimony he "has or likely will
offer." ECF No. 39 at 7. The Reply rested that proposition on procedural developments in the
underlying actions that came after the letters. The Opposition calls the proposition a "further
development" of the opening argument. The Opposition then adds a third formulation: Plaintiff's
claims "had not even survived initial motions to dismiss" when the letters issued. ECF No. 69 at 2-

3. The opening memorandum imposed neither requirement. Plaintiff has had no authorized
opportunity to answer either one.
Meta's remaining objection confirms the point. Meta faults the proposed sur-reply for
"simply reiterat[ing] allegations from the FAC." ECF No. 69 at 3. But the Reply asserts that the
FAC lacks sufficiently concrete prospective testimony. The direct answer to that assertion is the
FAC itself: Plaintiff's prospective-witness status, the subjects of his expected sworn testimony,
and Defendants' alleged knowledge and purpose concerning that testimony. The proposed sur-
reply identifies those allegations and addresses nothing else.
The Court should grant ECF No. 43 and deem the proposed Sur-Reply filed.
Date: September 17, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
